title: I must be an idiot, I would appreciate help
author: Dangerous_Three_8506
selftext:
I have been studying a lot over the past few weeks about AI and game design and am completely lost on a topic, 3D Modeling.

Are sites like Meshy and Tripo the only sources to generate a 3D model? I have been using Astra and can't for the life of me figure out how to create a decent model. They always look like crap, even with Astra Ultra. Is there a certain Prompt you tell Astra? Are you guys using Blender? Do we need to wait a year or two before ChatGPT and Blender can make a Monkey?

I am currently resorting to free Models available on the internet but I was hoping Astra could make a Monkey. This is what my monkey looks like.

https://preview.redd.it/63xg4a4ovyoh1.png?width=1000&format=png&auto=webp&s=de87f9c5ea516a1dabb3a532f118a48983c2ef47

comments.author: guanzo91
comments.body:
I'm in the same boat... tbh I feel deceived by the marketing around Astra's 3D modeling capabilities. 

I had it generate 3 different angles of a mech then told it to model with Blender MCP... the output was laughably bad. I don't have anything to show because I rage deleted the models last night lol.

I tried modeling individual body parts one at a time instead of all at once, still garbage.

I tried getting it to exhaustively list every single detail of the reference image, kind of like a textual specification of an image, hoping that Astra could check its work against the spec, but there's no way to maintain image fidelity with a text description. 

There's just no way for Astra to check its own work against the reference, it has no idea what it's making vs what it's supposed to be making.

Idk how other people were generating those beautiful models, but it's definitely not plug and play.

> Are sites like Meshy and Tripo the only sources to generate a 3D model?

Unfortunately i think so, and they all require payment in order to export the mesh. There must be open source models but who's shelling out $10k+ in order to actually run those?

Idk where to go from here, I guess I have to shell out some money for Meshy/Tripo...?

replies.author: PumpkinUpstairs
replies.body: As far as I know, it looks like Astra got nerfed; I read posts from people saying that, a few days after release, the same 3D model had been reworked and Astra had become trash.

replies.author: Dangerous_Three_8506
replies.body:
Im just sticking to Ai and free until my game is complete. Then ill do the art, whether its paying for individual or meshy.

That wont be for 1-3 years. Ai will improve by then anyways.

comments.author: Ok-Librarian-5223
comments.body: I use Hun yuan for models and tripo for texturing, and humanoids I rig in Realusion actor core

comments.author: CraigBMG
comments.body:
I've been using Tripo+Blender.  It has been hit and miss.  Maybe more miss.  
  
I have used Hunyuan locally in ComfyUI as well.  
  
For the most part, the meshes have been OK, but details have been uneven or distorted.  Smart Mesh seems like it should be good, and generating a quad mesh is nice, but it's hard to get something with good topology.  
  
Textures are another matter entirely.  The UV generation is a disaster area.  It generates dozens of little islands.  Mipmapping or even texture scaling seems to break horribly.    
  
I have had more luck UV unwrapping the mesh myself, then feeding that mesh back into Tripo and getting it to texture that.  Still not great, but I managed a decent cat model doing that - with a bunch of cleanup in Blender.

comments.author: EternalDreamIP
comments.body: How are you generating it? The easier and most accurate way is to: 1. Create an image of the model you want, specially in T pose 3 angle reference. 2. Give that image to Meshy, tripo or Hi3d, with the image to 3d model create. 3. Fix with Blender the higher mistakes (if so). Don't worry about the polygons, you can remesh with Meshy easily and free.
